timeline.jb: The tape is the whole case right now. What you put on film against SEC defenses is what scouts grade and what NIL partners look at.
Position work and strength. Where that happens is the player's call; an agent helps pick the room and keeps the eligibility paperwork clean.
Schools can pay players directly now, and outside deals of $600 or more get reviewed by the College Sports Commission. An agent's job here is reading the terms before anything gets signed.
Another year of SEC tape. Scouts start the conversations; the agent handles them so they don't get in the way of Saturdays.
Eligibility and the market set the timing. An honest read on both is the job, whichever way it points.
Combine or Pro Day, then draft weekend. The rookie contract is the first thing negotiated, drafted or signed after.

parentQA.a: Yes, when it is done in the open. NIL representation is governed by state law, NCAA rules and the school's own policy. We register where registration is required, every agreement goes in writing, and we file what the school asks for. If something would cost him eligibility, we do not do it.
Nothing up front. Our fee is a percentage of NIL and marketing income we bring in, stated in the agreement before anything is signed. We walk through the exact terms with you in person.
Ryan Hays, a licensed attorney and NFL contract advisor since 2012. Collective agreements, brand deals, exclusivity, what happens if a coach leaves. He reads all of it before your son signs.

parentQA.q: What if it isn't working at his school?
parentQA.a: Then we have a protocol for that. It is a last resort. The plan is to make it work where he is. If a move is ever the right call, it is made with a short list, a real need on the other end, and everything in writing.
Jack first, then Ryan. Both have his number, and there is no account manager in between.

In business since 1986, with six clients who became the highest paid at their position. Jack Tabb played the position, and Ryan Hays is a licensed attorney. We're happy to connect you with current client families.
